gaps.desktop: Checklist glyph on the 'Buy party decorations' row (about 19x22px, right of the notes glyph): the loser draws heavy filled bullets about 7px wide next to faint hairline dashes about 10px long, so at 1x it reads as a column of dots, and its notes glyph has a blobby filled dog-ear. The winner uses outlined ring bullets and dashes at the same ~1.5px stroke and ~#A8A8A8 tone, with a thin-line fold on the notes glyph, so both clearly read as checklist and notes. Redraw the loser's glyph with equal stroke weight for bullets and lines.
gaps.phone: Project subtitles (Vacation in Rome, Work, Plan Yearly Retreat and the rest) on every row: the loser sets them about 7 levels lighter (~#B4B4B4 vs the winner's ~#ADADAD on white). That drops already weak contrast to about 2:1 and makes the second line fade away under the black 17px titles. Darken the subtitle gray to the winner's ~#ADADAD (or a touch darker). The loser's 64px FAB also sits right beside the last row with only a ~17px bottom inset, where the winner leaves ~29px clear.

why: Near-identical geometry at both sizes (same 24px checkboxes, row pitch, heading and divider). Desktop is decided by the winner's cleaner, weight-matched notes and checklist glyphs; phone by the winner's stronger subtitle contrast and a FAB that stays clear of the rows.
